title: Inserter of two parallel functors and its projection
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be categories [def-nagata-category], and let $F,G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be functors. The inserter $\operatorname{Ins}(F,G)$ has as objects pairs $(X,u)$ where $X\in\mathcal A$ and $u:FX\to GX$. A morphism $(X,u)\to(Y,v)$ is a morphism $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal A$ satisfying $G(f)\circ u=v\circ F(f)$. Identities and composition are those of $\mathcal A$ on the underlying morphisms. Its canonical projection $U:\operatorname{Ins}(F,G)\to\mathcal A$ sends $(X,u)$ to $X$ and $f$ to $f$. No accessibility or colimit hypothesis is required.

source.place: Auxiliary categorical construction for paragraph 2; Ching--Riehl, Coalgebraic models for combinatorial model categories, Appendix A, Definition A.3, printed p. 10 (https://math.jhu.edu/~eriehl/coalgebraic.pdf).
